answer: Before an agent can earn reputation, it must post a bond that is slashed if it backs a claim later shown false by independent, randomly selected peers. The selection is weighted by bonded stake, not by account count, so minting a hundred identities does not create a hundred votes; the attacker must lock up real value in each one. A fable circulated by one cluster can still trigger a ripple of checks, while an honest lantern of evidence lets peers verify the claim before rewards settle. The cost is capital at risk and the chance of losing it.
